members.name: value
members.description: InputOTP forwards input-otp1.4.2 OTPInputProps, maxLength:number is required, value/defaultValue are strings, onChange(newValue:string) is not a native event callback. onComplete receives the complete value when a previously observed shorter value becomes exactly maxLength; initial full value is not an automatic completion request. It does not submit, verify, store or resend codes. The underlying library defaults inputMode=numeric and autoComplete=one-time-code, but only a supplied pattern enforces characters. This reference explicitly selects maxLength6 and REGEXP_ONLY_DIGITS, complete six slots indexed0..5, and a pasteTransformer removing spaces/hyphens. Pattern failure rejects the whole candidate rather than sanitizing arbitrary letters. Underlying selection, paste insertion, length truncation and fake caret use one actual input; slots/groups are visual divs. The reference explicitly hides visual slots and the separator from assistive technology while the real input remains labelled/exposed. Wrapper spellCheck=false can be overridden by native props. Disabled suppresses native user editing; controlled props remain authoritative and caller owns verification errors, cooldown and server response. The input-otp implementation also forwards native defaultValue alongside its internal value when supplied; React19 can warn about both. This reference deliberately uses the controlled string form.

events.name: onChange
events.description: Actual input-otp string callback, not a DOM event or cancellable BaseUI transaction.

events.name: onComplete
events.description: Exact upstream declaration; implementation passes the full string on the shorter-to-full transition, without verification or automatic submission.

cssParts.name: container
cssParts.description: Actual OTPInput containerClassName receives source cn-input-otp class; not six real inputs. Semantic adapter part; actual React selector/ownership is in component.partBindings, not a promised Shadow DOM export.

cssParts.name: input
cssParts.description: Single actual native input owns value, name, focus, paste and completion. Semantic adapter part; actual React selector/ownership is in component.partBindings, not a promised Shadow DOM export.
